headline: Congress cancels a 2024 federal land rule that had blocked new coal leasing in the Buffalo Field Office area of Wyoming.
what_it_does: This law uses the Congressional Review Act to cancel a Bureau of Land Management (BLM) rule from November 2024. That rule changed the land plan for the Buffalo Field Office in Wyoming so that no federal coal there could be leased in the future. With the rule canceled, the BLM must go back to its 2015 plan, which makes federal coal in the area available for leasing. The 2024 change had come after a court ruled that the BLM had to study climate effects and consider limiting or stopping coal leasing there.

who_it_affects.how: They can once again seek new leases for federal coal managed by the BLM in the Buffalo Field Office area.
The agency must follow its 2015 land plan for the area and treat federal coal as available for leasing.

who_it_affects.group: People and communities in the Buffalo Field Office area of Wyoming
who_it_affects.how: Federal coal land near them is again open to possible future leasing under the older plan.

when_it_takes_effect: December 11, 2025, when it was signed into law.
